texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 01.02.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 01.02.2023 at about 09.20 a.m., petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-51-H-8246 along with his friend Murugan on Big Banyan Tree Road, Ramohalli, Kengeri Hobli, Bangalore i.e., from Vinayaka Nagar and proceeding towards Big Banyan Tree. The rider of the said motorcycle riding slowly, cautiously and observing all the traffic norms on the extreme left side of the road. When he reached near Mukthinaga Temple Arch, Ramohalli, at that time all of a sudden a Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-41-C-7948 driving by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner without observing traffic norms and took sudden right turn without giving any hand signal or indicator and lost the control over his vehicle and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle. Due to the impact, the petitioner and the rider Murugan fell down on the road and petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his left leg and knee joint. Immediately, he was shifted to KOC Hospital for first aid and then he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment expenses. Ranganathan Kannan vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3953349/ 2 The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 30 years, the petitioner was working as Mason and earning Rs.45,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondents have appeared before the court through their counsels. The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 147, 149, 134(c) amd 158(6) of MV Act. Further this respondent submits that, the driver of Tipper Lorry was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident, hence this respondent is not obligated to indemnify the 2nd respondent. Further this respondent denies the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and involvement of the said vehicle in the alleged accident. The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 68 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.11 to the tune of Rs.1,22,898/-. Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,22,898/- towards medical expenses. 20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD: The petitioner has produced Ex. 21.
